mainTopic: יעקב's miraculous journey, the near-destruction of דוד's line, and the downfall of סנחריב's enormous army.
overview: This amud opens by finishing the proof that the land 'jumped' for יעקב, so that he suddenly arrived at the place where his fathers prayed. It then reads ויפגע as תפילה and explains that the sun set early so יעקב would sleep there, which was later balanced by the sun rising early for him. Next the גמרא shows that דוד's line was nearly wiped out by עתליה, and that יואש survived only because אביתר had survived the killing of the כהנים in נוב. The גמרא then describes the enormous army of סנחריב: its divisions, the size of its camp, and how it drained a river while crossing. It explains that the 185,000 struck by the מלאך were only the officers, and lists many opinions on how they were struck and how many survived. Finally, רבי אבהו brings the startling פסוק about ה׳ 'shaving' the king of אשור. The story behind it begins with ה׳ appearing to סנחריב as an old man, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The land jumped for יעקב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from the פסוקים that the land 'jumped' for יעקב. He wanted to go back and pray where his fathers had prayed, and he arrived there at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And יעקב left באר שבע and went toward חרן,' and it is written: 'And he reached the place and slept there, for the sun had set.' When he got to חרן he said: 'Could it be that I passed the place where my fathers prayed and I did not pray there?' He wanted to go back. As soon as he decided in his mind to go back, the land jumped for him. Right away: 'And he reached the place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is showing from the פסוקים that יעקב had קפיצת הדרך, meaning the land shrank under him so that he arrived far sooner than normal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק already has יעקב going toward חרן, yet the next פסוק says he 'reached the place,' which sounds sudden. The גמרא explains that he was already in חרן, regretted skipping the place of prayer, and the moment he decided to go back the land jumped and he was there at once.

keyTerms.meaning: The land 'jumped' (shrank) for him, so he arrived miraculously fast
He thought it over in his mind

steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the proof that יעקב belongs on the list of people for whom the land jumped.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And Jacob left Beersheba
phrases.notes: This proves יעקב was one of the people for whom the land jumped, continuing the list from just before. בראשית 28:10.

phrases.english: and went to Haran,'
and it is written: 'And he reached the place,
and he slept there, for the sun had set.'
When he arrived at Haran, he said:
Is it possible that I passed by a place
where my fathers prayed
and I did not pray there?
He wanted to go back.
As soon as he thought in his mind to go back,
the land jumped for him.
Immediately: 'And he reached the place.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier list of people for whom the land jumped, supplying the proof for יעקב.
steps.raayaObject: That the land jumped for יעקב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 28:10–11: he went toward חרן, then suddenly 'reached the place.'

steps.title: Another reading: reaching means praying
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation: the word פגיעה here means תפילה, as shown by a פסוק in ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'reaching' means nothing other than prayer, as it says: 'And you, do not pray for this nation, and do not raise for them song or prayer, and do not reach Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different meaning for ויפגע: it means יעקב prayed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ירמיהו, 'do not reach Me' sits right next to 'do not pray,' which shows that פגיעה can mean prayer. Read this way, 'ויפגע במקום' means יעקב prayed at that place.

keyTerms.meaning: Reaching / encountering; here read as prayer

phrases.english: Another explanation:
'reaching' means nothing other than prayer,
as it is stated: 'And you, do not pray
on behalf of this nation,
and do not raise on their behalf song and prayer,
and do not reach Me.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: אֵין פְּגִיעָה אֶלָּא תְּפִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second way to read the word ויפגע from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this פסוק, פגיעה means תפילה.

steps.title: The sun set early so יעקב would sleep there
steps.stepSummary: After יעקב prayed he wanted to move on, but הקדוש ברוך הוא made the sun set early so that he would stay the night.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he slept there, for the sun had set.' After he prayed, he wanted to go back. הקדוש ברוך הוא said: 'This righteous man came to My inn, and he should leave without staying the night?' Immediately the sun set.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the words 'for the sun had set': the sunset was arranged early by הקדוש ברוך הוא so that יעקב would sleep at that place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'כי בא השמש' is read as a special act, not a normal sunset. הקדוש ברוך הוא treated the place as His 'inn' and did not want His guest to leave without staying the night.

phrases.english: 'And he slept there, for the sun had set.'
After he prayed, he wanted to go back,
phrases.notes: Here 'go back' means returning to his journey to חרן.

phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
This righteous man came to My inn,
and he should leave without staying the night?
Immediately the sun set.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next words of the same פסוק and explains them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sun set early, out of its normal time, so that יעקב would stay the night.

steps.title: Support from 'the sun shone for him'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects the early sunset to a later פסוק that says the sun shone 'for him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what is written: 'And the sun shone for him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a later פסוק about יעקב as a hint to the early-sunset story. It is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'for him' suggest that the sunrise was special to יעקב. The גמרא links this to the earlier special sunset, but the exact link is explained only after the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what is written

phrases.english: And this is what is written:
'And the sun shone for him.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 32:32, when יעקב was coming back years later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 3 with another פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That the sun behaved in a special way for יעקב.

steps.title: Did the sun shine only for him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording: the sun shines for the whole world, so why does the פסוק say 'for him'?
steps.simpleTranslation: Did it shine only for him? It shone for the entire world!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the words 'for him' in the פסוק, since the sunrise is not private to one person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every sunrise lights up the whole world, so 'for him' seems like extra wording. The question forces us to find a special meaning in these words.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it so that...? (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: And did it shine only for him?
But it shone for the entire world!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the פסוק brought in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'לו' (for him) in ויזרח לו השמש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sun rises for everyone, so 'for him' seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Rabbi Yitzchak: the early sunset was balanced by an early sunrise
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains that the sun which set early for יעקב's sake later rose early for his sake.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יצחק said: The sun that set because of him rose because of him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the question: 'for him' means the sun rose early for יעקב's sake, to balance the early sunset that was also for his sake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The early sunset in step 3 threw off the normal timing. 'ויזרח לו' teaches that the sun later made up for it by rising early, also because of יעקב. That ties the two פסוקים together.

keyTerms.meaning: For his sake / because of him

steps.whatToRemember: The sun set early for יעקב so that he would sleep at the holy place, and later it rose early for him to even things out. That is the meaning of 'ויזרח לו השמש.'

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yitzchak said:
The sun that set for his sake
shone (rose) for his sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'For him' looks pointless, since the sun shines for everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'For him' refers to the early sunrise that made up for the early sunset caused for יעקב's sake.

steps.title: How do we know David's line was wiped out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to דוד and asks for the source that his descendants were nearly destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that דוד's descendants were wiped out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier discussion about דוד and asks for a source that his family line came to an end. This sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on this daf, דוד's family line was said to be destroyed as a punishment. Now the גמרא wants to see where that actually happened in the פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?

phrases.english: And from where do we know that David's descendants were wiped out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the יעקב discussion and returns to the earlier topic of דוד.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that דוד's descendants were destroyed.

steps.title: Athaliah destroyed the royal family
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק about עתליה killing all the royal descendants.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And עתליה, the mother of אחזיהו, saw that her son was dead, and she rose and destroyed all the royal descendants.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק: עתליה killed all of the royal family, who were דוד's descendants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The royal family of יהודה came from דוד. So when עתליה destroyed 'all the royal descendants,' that is דוד's line being wiped out.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah,
saw that her son was dead,
and she rose and destroyed
all the royal descendants.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מלכים ב 11:1: עתליה destroyed all the royal descendants.

steps.title: But Yoash survived
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: יואש survived, so the line was not fully wiped out.
steps.simpleTranslation: But יואש remained alive!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof: one of דוד's descendants, יואש, escaped, so the line did not completely end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even one descendant survived, it seems wrong to say the line 'ended.' The challenge questions whether the punishment really happened in full.

phrases.english: But didn't Joash remain for him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that דוד's line was wiped out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יואש survived עתליה's massacre, so the line was not completely destroyed.

steps.title: In Nov too, one survivor remained
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that at the killing of the כהנים in נוב one person also survived, אביתר. So one survivor here matches one survivor there.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, אביתר remained, as it is written: 'And one son of אחימלך the son of אחיטוב escaped, and his name was אביתר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the punishment matched the original sin, and in the original massacre at נוב one person also escaped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד's punishment was tied to the killing of the כהנים of נוב. Since one כהן, אביתר, escaped there, one descendant of דוד, יואש, escaped here. The survival of יואש fits the punishment instead of disproving it.

phrases.english: There too, Abiathar remained,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the killing of the כהנים in נוב, which דוד's punishment was connected to.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'And one son escaped
of Ahimelech, son of Ahitub,
and his name was Abiathar.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallel between the punishment and the sin
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יואש's survival shows that דוד's line was not wiped out.
steps.terutzMaskana: One survivor at נוב (אביתר) is matched by one survivor of דוד's line (יואש).

steps.title: רב: without Evyatar, nothing of David would remain
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב states that if אביתר had not survived, not a single descendant of דוד would have survived.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: If אביתר had not survived for אחימלך the son of אחיטוב, not a single survivor or refugee would have remained of דוד's descendants.
steps.whatsHappening: רב confirms the answer: דוד's line survived only because אביתר survived at נוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This states outright what step 10 suggested: the survival of דוד's line depended completely on the survival of אביתר. Without him, דוד's line would have been completely destroyed.

keyTerms.meaning: Were it not that / if not for
A survivor and a refugee (not even one left)

steps.whatToRemember: דוד's line was nearly destroyed by עתליה. One descendant, יואש, survived only because one כהן, אביתר, had survived the massacre at נוב.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Were it not that Abiathar remained
for Ahimelech, son of Ahitub,
there would not have remained of the descendants of David
a survivor or a refugee.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: אִלְמָלֵא לֹא נִשְׁתַּיֵּיר אֶבְיָתָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up and states clearly the answer given in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The survival of יואש, the one remnant of דוד's line, depended entirely on אביתר's survival at נוב.

steps.title: רב describes the makeup of Sennacherib's army
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב describes the army סנחריב brought: princes in golden carriages, armored warriors, sword-bearers and horsemen. Armies this size also came against אברהם and will come with גוג ומגוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The wicked סנחריב came against them with 45,000 princes riding in golden carriages, with women alongside them. He also brought 80,000 warriors in armor and 60,000 sword-bearers running before him. All the rest were horsemen. Armies just like this came against אברהם, and armies like this will come with גוג ומגוג.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: a description by רב of how big and grand the army of סנחריב was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב lists the army in groups: 45,000 princes, 80,000 armored warriors, 60,000 sword-bearers, and the rest horsemen. He then links this army to two others, the kings who fought אברהם and the future war of גוג ומגוג, which were just as large.

keyTerms.meaning: The king of אשור who attacked ירושלים
The nations of the great war at the end of days

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Sennacherib the wicked came upon them
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the Jews of ירושלים, whom סנחריב attacked.

phrases.aramaic: בְּאַרְבָּעִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה אֶלֶף אִישׁ בְּנֵי מְלָכִים,
phrases.english: with forty-five thousand men, sons of kings,
sitting in carriages of gold,
and with them were consorts and prostitutes,
and with eighty thousand warriors
wearing coats of armor,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְשִׁשִּׁים אֶלֶף אֲחוּזֵי חֶרֶב רָצִים לְפָנָיו,
phrases.english: and with sixty thousand sword-bearers running before him,
and the rest were horsemen.
And likewise they came upon Avraham,
phrases.notes: This is the war of the four kings in בראשית 14.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן עֲתִידִין לָבוֹא עִם גּוֹג וּמָגוֹג.
phrases.english: and likewise they are destined to come with Gog and Magog.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: בָּא עֲלֵיהֶם סַנְחֵרִיב הָרָשָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from דוד's descendants to a new description of סנחריב's army.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סנחריב's army had 45,000 princes, 80,000 armored warriors, 60,000 sword-bearers and the rest horsemen. Armies this size came against אברהם and will come with גוג ומגוג.

steps.title: A baraita gives the size of the camp
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the camp was 400 פרסה long, the horses' necks lined up side by side measured 40 פרסה, and the total was 260 myriads of thousands minus one.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: His camp was 400 פרסה long. His horses standing neck to neck stretched 40 פרסה wide. The total size of his army was 260 myriads of thousands, minus one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds exact measurements and a total number for סנחריב's army. This total sets up אביי's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב only listed groups of soldiers. The ברייתא adds the physical size of the camp and a grand total. The total ends with the unclear words 'minus one', which leads straight into the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A large measure of distance, about 4 מיל

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
The length of his camp was four hundred parasangs,
the width of the necks of his horses was forty parasangs.
phrases.notes: He means the horses standing neck to neck, side by side.

phrases.english: The total of his camp

phrases.aramaic: מָאתַיִם וְשִׁשִּׁים רִיבּוֹא אֲלָפִים חָסֵר חַד.
phrases.english: was two hundred and sixty myriads of thousands, minus one.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא: אוֹרֶךְ מַחֲנֵהוּ אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת פַּרְסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא with measurements and a total to רב's description.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The camp was 400 פרסה long and 40 פרסה wide at the horses' necks. The total was 260 myriads of thousands minus one.

steps.title: אביי asks what 'minus one' means, and it stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks whether 'minus one' means minus ten thousand, a thousand, a hundred, or just one person. The question is left as תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked: Does 'minus one' mean minus one ten-thousand, minus one thousand, minus one hundred, or just minus one person? The question stands unanswered (תיקו).
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks what the ברייתא means by 'minus one'. The גמרא has no answer and leaves it as תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the ברייתא counts in big units, 'one' might mean one of those units, or it might mean a single soldier. אביי lists the four options, and since no source settles it, the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question is left unresolved

phrases.english: Abaye asked:
Is it minus one ten-thousand,
or minus one thousand,
or minus a hundred,
or minus one person?
Let it stand.
phrases.notes: No answer is found, so the question is left open.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the words 'minus one' in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What unit does 'minus one' refer to: ten thousand, a thousand, a hundred, or one person?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: None. The question stays as תיקו.

steps.title: How the army drained the river as it crossed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the first soldiers swam across, the middle ones walked through standing, and the last ones kicked up dust and had to bring water from elsewhere. Each stage is tied to a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: The first soldiers crossed by swimming, as the פסוק says, 'He shall sweep through Yehuda, overflowing and passing.' The middle ones crossed standing up, as it says, 'It shall reach up to the neck.' The last ones kicked up dust with their feet and found no water to drink in the river, until they brought water from somewhere else, as it says, 'I dug and drank water.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another ברייתא shows how huge the army was: so many soldiers crossed that they used up the whole river.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water dropped in three stages: deep enough to swim, then up to the neck, then totally dry. Each stage is matched to a phrase in ישעיהו. It is another way of showing the army's enormous size.

phrases.english: It was taught:
The first ones crossed by swimming,
as it is said: "And he shall sweep through Yehuda, overflowing and passing."
The middle ones crossed standing upright,
as it is said: "It shall reach up to the neck."
The last ones raised dust with their feet
and did not find water in the river to drink,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁהֵבִיאוּ מַיִם מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר וְשָׁתוּ,
phrases.english: until they brought water from another place and drank,
as it is said: "I dug and drank water, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another ברייתא showing the army's size through its crossing of the river.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The army was so large that the river went from swimming depth, to neck depth, to completely dry as it crossed.

steps.title: Challenge: the פסוק says only 185,000 died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects from the פסוק that the מלאך struck 185,000 in the camp of אשור and all were dead. That number seems far smaller than the huge army described.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the פסוק says: 'The angel of ה׳ went out and struck 185,000 in the camp of אשור, and in the morning they were all dead.' That sounds like the whole army was only 185,000!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the huge numbers from the פסוק that says the whole camp was 185,000 people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 185,000 were struck and then 'they were all' dead, which sounds like 185,000 was the entire army. That clashes with the ברייתא's total of millions.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (introduces a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"And the angel of ה׳ went out
and struck in the camp of Ashur
one hundred and eighty-five thousand,
and they rose early in the morning,
and behold, they were all dead corpses"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכְתִיב: ״וַיֵּצֵא מַלְאַךְ ה׳ וַיַּכֶּה בְּמַחֲנֵה אַשּׁוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the army sizes given in the previous steps.
steps.kashyaTarget: The huge army numbers given by רב and the ברייתות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says 185,000 were struck and 'all' were dead, which suggests the whole army was only 185,000.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: the 185,000 were officers
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that the 185,000 in the פסוק were the heads of the regiments, each leading many soldiers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: Those 185,000 were the heads of regiments.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the challenge: the פסוק only counts the officers, not every soldier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 185,000 were commanders, and each one led many soldiers under him. So the פסוק and the huge total in the ברייתא do not clash.
steps.whatToRemember: סנחריב's army was enormous; the 185,000 in the פסוק were only its officers.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
These were heads of regiments.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: הַלָּלוּ רָאשֵׁי גְיָיסוֹת הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets who is being counted in the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 185,000 in the פסוק were the whole army.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 185,000 were only the regiment commanders, so the total army was far larger.

steps.title: רב אשי brings support from 'among his fat ones'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי supports רבי אבהו's answer from the פסוק 'במשמניו רזון', which means the important ones among them were struck.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי says: The פסוק also shows this, because it says 'among his fat ones, leanness.' That means the 'fat' ones among them, the important people.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a פסוק to back up רבי אבהו's answer from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not say the whole army was struck. It says 'his fat ones', and 'fat' here means the important people. That fits רבי אבהו's point that the 185,000 who died were the leaders.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also precise: the wording of a source also supports this
Among his fat ones, meaning his important people

phrases.english: Rav Ashi says: It is also precise,
as it is written: "Among his fat ones, leanness"
meaning, the fat ones who are among them.
phrases.notes: "Fat" here means the important ones, the leaders of the army.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אבהו's answer in step 17
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבהו's claim that the 185,000 were regiment heads

steps.title: רבינא brings support from 'every leader and officer'
steps.stepSummary: רבינא supports the same idea from a פסוק in דברי הימים that lists warriors, leaders and officers. The גמרא accepts the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא says: The wording also shows this, because it says 'ה' sent a מלאך, who destroyed every mighty warrior, leader and officer in the camp... and when he came into the house of his god, his own sons struck him down there with the sword.' The גמרא concludes: learn from this that it was the leaders who were killed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a second פסוק that supports רבי אבהו, and the גמרא accepts it with 'שמע מינה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק names who was destroyed: warriors, leaders and officers. That is a list of important people, not ordinary soldiers. So the proof is accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: Conclude from it: the proof is accepted

phrases.english: Ravina says: It is also precise,
as it is written: "And the Lord sent an angel,
and he destroyed every mighty warrior
and leader and officer in the camp, etc.
And he came into the house of his god,
and those who came out of his body
struck him down there with the sword."
Conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second proof for the same answer, ending with acceptance
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבהו's claim that the 185,000 were leaders
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים ב 32:21, which lists warriors, leaders and officers
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The 185,000 killed were the leaders, so the army itself really was enormous.
steps.whatToRemember: The problem from step 16 is solved: the 185,000 were only the leaders, and each one led a huge number of soldiers.

steps.title: With what were they struck?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the army of סנחריב was struck.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what did He strike them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about how the army was killed. This sets up the list of answers that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know who died, the גמרא turns to how they died. Many opinions follow, and each one is tied to a פסוק.

phrases.english: With what did He strike them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who was killed to how they were killed
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The way the army of אשור was destroyed

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: struck by the hand
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says they were struck by God's hand, the 'great hand' that was saved for punishing סנחריב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: He struck them with the hand, as it says: 'And Israel saw the great hand.' This is the hand that was going to punish סנחריב in the future.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives the first answer: God struck them with His 'hand'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק at the Sea says 'THE great hand', with the word 'the'. רבי אליעזר reads this as a specific hand that would later be used against סנחריב.

keyTerms.meaning: To punish, to collect payment for wrongs

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: He struck them with the hand,
as it is stated: "And Israel saw the great hand."
The hand that was destined to punish Sennacherib.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question

steps.title: רבי יהושע: struck by the finger
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says they were struck by God's finger, the same 'finger of God' mentioned in מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: He struck them with the finger, as it says: 'The magicians said to פרעה: This is the finger of God.' That is the finger that was going to punish סנחריב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע gives a second answer: only God's 'finger' was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע uses the פסוק from the plagues in מצרים. He says that same 'finger' was waiting to punish סנחריב, and a finger is even less than a whole hand.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: He struck them with the finger,
as it is stated: "And the magicians said to Pharaoh:
This is the finger of God."
That is the finger that was destined to punish Sennacherib.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer than רבי אליעזר

steps.title: Gabriel's sickle has been sharp since Creation
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר the son of רבי יוסי הגלילי says that הקדוש ברוך הוא asked גבריאל if his sickle was sharpened, and גבריאל answered it had been ready since the six days of Creation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר the son of רבי יוסי הגלילי says: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to גבריאל: Is your sickle sharpened? He said before Him: Master of the World, it has been standing sharpened since the six days of Creation, as it says: 'from the sharpened sword, from the bent bow, from the heaviness of war.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer: the army was killed by גבריאל using his sickle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the killing is done by the מלאך גבריאל, not directly by God's 'hand' or 'finger'. The פסוק about a 'sharpened sword' is read as גבריאל's blade, ready from the beginning of the world.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, says:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְגַבְרִיאֵל:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Gabriel:
Is your sickle sharpened?
He said before Him: Master of the World,
it has stood sharpened since the six days of Creation,
as it is stated: "From the sharpened sword,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי קֶשֶׁת דְּרוּכָה מִפְּנֵי כּוֹבֶד מִלְחָמָה] (וְגוֹ)״.
phrases.english: from the bent bow, from the heaviness of war" (etc.).
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 21:15. The words in square brackets are the corrected wording, spelling out the rest of the פסוק; it leaves out the "etc." in round brackets.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third answer: through גבריאל and his sickle
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: By גבריאל's sickle, which had been sharp since Creation

steps.title: Gabriel strikes them on his way to ripen fruit
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says it was fruit-ripening season, and God told גבריאל to deal with the army while he was out ripening the fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says: That time was the season for ripening fruit. הקדוש ברוך הוא said to גבריאל: When you go out to ripen the fruit, take care of them too, as it says: 'Whenever it passes through, it will take you, for every morning it will pass, by day and by night, and just understanding the report will bring terror.'
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth answer: גבריאל destroyed the army as a side job while he was busy ripening fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that destroying this huge army was not even a special mission. גבריאל did it 'in passing', and the פסוק 'whenever it passes through, it will take you' is read this way.

keyTerms.meaning: Take care of them, deal with them

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai says:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתוֹ הַפֶּרֶק זְמַן בִּישּׁוּל פֵּירוֹת הָיָה.
phrases.english: That period was the season of the ripening of fruit.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְגַבְרִיאֵל:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Gabriel:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁאַתָּה יוֹצֵא לְבַשֵּׁל פֵּירוֹת, הִזָּקֵק לָהֶם,
phrases.english: When you go out to ripen the fruit, deal with them,
as it is stated: "Whenever it passes through, it shall take you,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי בַבֹּקֶר בַּבֹּקֶר יַעֲבֹר בַּיּוֹם וּבַלָּיְלָה
phrases.english: for morning by morning it shall pass through, by day and by night,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיָה רַק זְוָעָה הָבִין שְׁמוּעָה וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: and the mere understanding of the report shall bring terror, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר: אוֹתוֹ הַפֶּרֶק זְמַן בִּישּׁוּל פֵּירוֹת הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth answer: גבריאל struck them while doing another job
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: גבריאל destroyed them on his way to ripen fruit

steps.title: רב פפא: 'on your way, show yourself to your enemy'
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא connects רבי שמעון בן יוחי's teaching to a popular saying: while you are on your way, show yourself to your enemy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says: This is what people say: On your way, let yourself be seen by your enemy.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a folk saying that matches the idea of the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He adds no new opinion about how they died. He shows that the idea of handling an enemy 'in passing', while busy with something else, matches a common saying.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say: a popular saying

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa says: This is what people say:
Along your way, let yourself be seen by your enemy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a popular saying that matches step 24
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dealing with an enemy in passing matches the popular saying.

steps.title: Some say: He blew into their noses
steps.stepSummary: Some say the army died when He blew into their noses.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: He blew into their noses and they died, as it says: 'He just blew on them, and they dried up.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another answer: the army died from a blow of breath into their noses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'He blew on them and they withered.' This is read as a breath that killed them, with no weapon at all.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: בְּחוֹטְמָן נָשַׁף בָּהֶן וָמֵתוּ,
phrases.english: And some say: He blew into their noses and they died,
as it is stated: "And He also blew upon them, and they withered."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: בְּחוֹטְמָן נָשַׁף בָּהֶן וָמֵתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer to the question

steps.title: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba: He clapped His hands
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא says He clapped His hands at them and they died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר אבא says: He clapped hands at them and they died, as it says: 'I too will strike My hand against My hand, and I will calm My anger.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another answer: a clap of the hands killed the army.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of striking hand against hand to let out anger. רבי ירמיה בר אבא reads this as the act that killed the army of אשור.

keyTerms.meaning: And I will calm My anger

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר: כַּפַּיִים סָפַק לָהֶם וָמֵתוּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba says: He clapped hands at them and they died,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְגַם אֲנִי אַכֶּה כַפִּי אֶל כַּפִּי
phrases.english: as it is stated: "I will also strike My hand against My hand,
and I will calm My anger."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר: כַּפַּיִים סָפַק לָהֶם וָמֵתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer to the question

steps.title: Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha: they heard the angels' song and died
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא says He opened their ears so they heard the song of the חיות, and they died from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא says: He opened ears for them, and they heard song from the mouths of the חיות, and they died, as it says: 'From Your greatness the nations were scattered.'
steps.whatsHappening: The last answer: the soldiers were allowed to hear the song of the heavenly creatures, and that alone killed them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normal people cannot hear the song of the חיות. Their ears were opened, and the greatness of God that they heard was too much for them. The פסוק 'from Your greatness the nations were scattered' is the source.

keyTerms.meaning: He opened their ears so they could hear
The holy creatures who carry God's chariot

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא brings many opinions on how the army of סנחריב was struck: hand, finger, גבריאל's sickle, גבריאל on his way to ripen fruit, a breath, a clap, or the song of the חיות. Each one is built on a פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא אָמַר: אׇזְנַיִם גָּלָה לָהֶם
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak Nappaḥa says: He opened ears for them,
and they heard song from the mouths of the holy creatures, and they died,
as it is stated: "From Your greatness the nations were scattered."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא אָמַר: אׇזְנַיִם גָּלָה לָהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final answer in the list
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They heard the song of the חיות and died

steps.title: How many soldiers survived?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how many of סנחריב's soldiers were left alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: How many of them were left?
steps.whatsHappening: After describing how the army died, the גמרא asks how many soldiers survived. This sets up a list of opinions that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps explained how the soldiers died. Now the focus moves to the survivors, and each answer will be built on a פסוק.

phrases.english: And how many of them remained?
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the soldiers of סנחריב's army.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how the army died to how many survived.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The number of soldiers who survived.

steps.title: רב: ten survived
steps.stepSummary: רב says ten survived, because a פסוק says a child could write their number.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says ten, because the פסוק says 'the rest of the trees of his forest will be few, a child could write them.' What number can a child write? Ten.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that ten soldiers survived and brings a פסוק from ישעיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says so few will be left that a young child could write their number. רב reasons that ten is the number a child can easily write, so ten survived.

keyTerms.meaning: his forest (a picture for the army)

phrases.english: Rav says: Ten,
as it is stated: “And the rest of the trees of his forest
shall be few, that a child may write them.”
What number can a child write? Ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of how many survived.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Ten survived, based on 'a child may write them.'

steps.title: שמואל: nine survived
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says nine survived, based on a פסוק about a few olives left on a tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל says nine, because the פסוק speaks of leftover olives after the tree is beaten: two or three at the top, four or five on the branches.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל disagrees with רב and says nine survived, using a different פסוק from ישעיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares the survivors to the few olives left after a harvest. שמואל reads a total of nine from the numbers in the פסוק, apparently four plus five.

phrases.english: And Shmuel says: Nine,
as it is stated: “And gleanings shall be left of him,
as in the beating of an olive tree,
two or three berries in the top of the uppermost bough,
four or five in its branches.”
phrases.notes: שמואל seems to get nine by adding four and five.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second opinion that argues with רב.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Nine survived, based on the olive-tree פסוק.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: fourteen survived
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי uses the same פסוק as שמואל but adds up all the numbers to get fourteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי says fourteen, because the פסוק says 'two, three, four and five.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion: רבי יהושע בן לוי reads the same olive פסוק and gets fourteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He adds every number in the פסוק together: 2+3+4+5 = 14. So he and שמואל share the same source but read it differently.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר: אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: Fourteen,
as it is stated: “Two, three… four and five.”
phrases.notes: Add them all up: 2+3+4+5 = 14. The word in square brackets just means 'and so on.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר: אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses שמואל's פסוק but counts it differently.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Fourteen survived, adding every number in the פסוק.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: five survived, and he names them
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says five survived: סנחריב, his two sons, נבוכדנצר, and נבוזראדן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says five: סנחריב and his two sons, נבוכדנצר and נבוזראדן.
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth opinion: רבי יוחנן says five survived, and he lists who they were by name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the others, רבי יוחנן does not start from a counting פסוק. He identifies specific people who appear later in תנ״ך, which shows they were still alive.

keyTerms.meaning: the king of Assyria who attacked ירושלים

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Five –
Sennacherib and his two sons,
Nebuchadnezzar and Nebuzaradan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth number, given with names instead of a counting פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Five survived: סנחריב, his two sons, נבוכדנצר, נבוזראדן.

steps.title: Proof for each of the five survivors
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows where we know each of רבי יוחנן's five survivors was there and lived.
steps.simpleTranslation: נבוזראדן we know from tradition. נבוכדנצר, because he later said 'the fourth one looks like an angel' — how would he know, unless he had seen one? סנחריב and his two sons, because the פסוק says his sons later killed him while he was bowing to his idol.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי יוחנן's list, giving a source for each name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For נבוזראדן there is only a received tradition. For נבוכדנצר, his ability to recognize an angel in דניאל proves he had seen the angel that struck סנחריב's army. For סנחריב and his sons, a פסוק describes them alive afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: a received tradition (here, not a פסוק)
and if he had not seen him

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's five survivors each have a source: tradition for נבוזראדן, דניאל for נבוכדנצר, and מלכים for סנחריב and his sons.

phrases.english: Nebuzaradan – from tradition.
Nebuchadnezzar – as it is written:
“And the appearance of the fourth
phrases.notes: דניאל 3:25. He said this when he saw a fourth figure in the fire with חנניה, מישאל and עזריה.

phrases.english: is like that of an angel.”
And if he had not seen him,
phrases.notes: Meaning the angel that struck סנחריב's army.

phrases.english: from where would he have known?
Sennacherib and his two sons – as it is written:
“And it came to pass as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god,
that Adrammelech and Sarezer, his sons,
struck him with the sword.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports each name in רבי יוחנן's list.
steps.raayaObject: That these five people survived the plague.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: a פסוק we could never say on our own
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says that if the פסוק were not written, we could not dare say that ה׳ Himself would 'shave' the king of Assyria.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: If the פסוק weren't written, we couldn't say it. It says: 'On that day ה׳ will shave with a hired razor, beyond the river, the king of Assyria — the head, the hair of the legs, and the beard too.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו brings a startling פסוק describing ה׳ as a barber shaving סנחריב. This sets up the story that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picturing ה׳ as a barber sounds disrespectful, so רבי אבהו says only the פסוק itself lets us say it. The גמרא will now tell a story explaining what this shaving was.

keyTerms.meaning: if the פסוק were not written
it would be impossible to say it

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu says:
Were the verse not written,
it would be impossible to say it,
phrases.notes: Because describing ה׳ as a barber sounds disrespectful.

phrases.english: as it is written: “On that day the Lord shall shave
with a hired razor, in the parts beyond the river,
the king of Assyria,
the head and the hair of the legs,
and it shall also sweep away the beard.”

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: אִלְמָלֵא מִקְרָא כָּתוּב, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְאׇמְרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about what happened to סנחריב himself after the plague.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק describes ה׳ shaving סנחריב — something we could only say because it is written.

steps.title: ה׳ appears to סנחריב as an old man
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ appears to סנחריב as an old man and asks what he will tell the kings whose sons died in his army.
steps.simpleTranslation: ה׳ came and looked to him like an old man. He said: When you go to the kings of the east and west, whose sons you brought and got killed, what will you tell them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts the story behind רבי אבהו's פסוק. ה׳, disguised as an old man, puts a hard question to סנחריב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סנחריב's army included the sons of many kings, and they all died. The old man's question points out that סנחריב now faces those angry fathers.

keyTerms.meaning: the Holy One, Blessed be He
kings of the east and west

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, came,
and appeared to him as an old man.
He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָזְלַתְּ לְגַבֵּי מַלְכֵי מִזְרָח וּמַעֲרָב
phrases.english: When you go to the kings of the east and the west
whose sons you brought and had killed,
what will you say to them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא, וְאִדְּמִי לֵיהּ כְּגַבְרָא סָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the story that explains רבי אבהו's פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳, disguised as an old man, confronts סנחריב about the kings' dead sons.

steps.title: סנחריב admits his fear and asks what to do
steps.stepSummary: סנחריב admits he is terrified too and asks the old man what to do; the old man begins his advice: 'Go.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: 'That man' (meaning himself) is sitting in that same fear. He asked: What should we do? He answered: Go…
steps.whatsHappening: סנחריב answers that he has no idea what to say and is afraid. He asks for advice, and the old man starts to answer — the advice continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סנחריב does not say 'I' but 'that man,' a polite way of talking about himself. His question 'what should we do' opens the door for the old man's plan, which leads into the 'shaving' of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: 'that man' — a polite way of saying 'I'

steps.confusionAlert: 'That man' is not someone else — סנחריב is talking about himself in a roundabout way.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הַהוּא גַּבְרָא בְּהָהוּא פַּחְדָּא נָמֵי יָתֵיב.
phrases.english: That man also sits in that very fear.
phrases.notes: סנחריב means himself: 'I'm afraid of that too.'

phrases.english: He said to him: What should we do?
He said to him: Go

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַהוּא גַּבְרָא בְּהָהוּא פַּחְדָּא נָמֵי יָתֵיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: סנחריב answers the old man's question and asks for advice.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סנחריב admits he is afraid and has nothing to say; the old man begins his advice.
